- issues opened in `experiment-repo`#8 ("Sparse matrix: add coverage-matched random and most-observed selectors") by `idea-review-repo`  > From idea-review (full review: story-repo#5, Q1). One extra baseline would settle what the sparse-matrix result means.
  > 
  > In `bmk/sparse.py` the random selector draws from the candidate set C, which includes benchmarks observed for few training models. Greedy A on the fitted covariance will tend to avoid thinly observed columns, so "greedy A beats random at every k" could be a coverage effect rather than an information effect.
  > 
  > Request: on the same partitions and folds, add (a) a coverage-matched random selector (random draw weighted by, or restricted to, the benchmarks with the most observed training cells) and (b) a "most-observed-k" selector, both with the `fa` and `pw` predictors, and report the greedy-minus-baseline gap with the same family-clustered CI. Either outcome is publishable; it changes whether the paper may say the gain is from information. Not needed for the dense pools. Novelty note: I did not search for the forbidden study.
